target.title: fix(agents): deliberate fallback for malformed compaction boundary timestamps
target.body:
## Summary

- Fix classification: Root-cause fix for compaction boundary timestamp validation.
- Maintainer-ready confidence: High after focused regressions, typecheck, real compaction-path proof, and build verification.
- Root cause: `checkCompaction()` parsed `compactionEntry.timestamp` with `new Date(...).getTime()` without validating the result. An unparseable timestamp returns `NaN`, and `<= NaN` always evaluates to `false` in JavaScript — silently deactivating the pre-compaction guard.
- Why this is a root-cause fix: the timestamp→epoch-ms contract is now enforced through a single `resolveCompactionTime()` helper. Invalid strings return `undefined` instead of `NaN`, and callers use an explicit `!== undefined` check instead of the fragile `!Number.isNaN()` pattern.
- Dependency graph status: no dependency changes. The helper lives in `compaction-time.ts`, an internal module not re-exported from the public plugin SDK.

## Linked context

- Linked issue: #99444 — "guard NaN timestamp in compaction boundary check".
- Out of scope: no migration/backfill for historical compaction entries, no change to compaction logic beyond the timestamp guard, no new dependency, no config or schema changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99444: `checkCompaction()` (`src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts`) parsed `compactionEntry.timestamp` with `new Date(...).getTime()` at two call sites. An unparseable timestamp returns `NaN`, and `<= NaN` always evaluates to `false`, so:

1. `assistantIsFromBeforeCompaction` never activates → stale pre-compaction messages re-trigger compaction
2. Usage-message staleness check silently fails → stale usage data can falsely trigger post-compaction compaction

## Root Cause

The old code used `Number.NaN` as an implicit sentinel and checked with `!Number.isNaN()`:

```ts
// Before: NaN sentinel — intent is hidden
compactionEntry !== null && !Number.isNaN(compactionTime) && timestamp <= compactionTime
```

This conflated "no entry" with "unparseable timestamp", and the lint rule `unicorn/prefer-number-properties` rejects the global `NaN`. More importantly, the guard's behavior when `NaN` is encountered is implicit — it relies on the JS language semantics of `<= NaN` being `false`.

## Strategy: Deliberate Fallback

When the compaction entry timestamp is unparseable, the boundary is **treated as unreliable** and the guard is skipped so compaction is checked normally. This is a deliberate fallback: a missing guard may trigger one extra compaction cycle, but a stuck guard would silently suppress compaction forever.

The new `resolveCompactionTime()` helper returns `number | undefined`:
- `null` entry → `undefined` (no boundary)
- Valid ISO timestamp → epoch ms
- Unparseable timestamp → `undefined` (boundary unreliable)

Callers check `compactionTime !== undefined` — explicit intent, no sentinel, no lint violation.

## Why This Change Was Made

| Scenario | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Valid timestamp | Guard works correctly | Guard works correctly (unchanged) |
| `null` compactionEntry | Guard skipped → check compaction | Guard skipped → check compaction (unchanged) |
| **Malformed timestamp** | `NaN` → `<= NaN` → `false` → guard silently skipped | `undefined` → `!== undefined` → `false` → guard explicitly skipped |

The behavioral outcome is the same for malformed timestamps (proceed to check compaction — the safe default), but the intent is now explicit and the `Number.NaN` sentinel is eliminated.

## User Impact

- Malformed compaction entry timestamps no longer silently suppress the pre-compaction guard
- One extra compaction cycle at worst (vs. runaway context growth at worst before)
- No `Number.NaN` lint violations
- Transparent to users; no config or behavior changes in the normal path

## What did NOT change

- Compaction logic beyond the timestamp guard
- Compaction settings, thresholds, or overflow recovery
- Session transcript format or storage
- Config defaults, schema files, or provider behavior
- No new public plugin SDK API surface

## Changes

- `src/agents/sessions/compaction-time.ts`: +18 lines (new file)
  - `resolveCompactionTime()` helper: returns `number | undefined`, handles null entry and `Number.isNaN()` fallback
  - Not re-exported from `index.ts` — stays off the public SDK surface
- `src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts`: +16 −4 lines
  - Imports `resolveCompactionTime` from the internal module
  - Both call sites: `compactionTime !== undefined` instead of old pattern
- `src/agents/sessions/agent-session.resolve-compaction-time.test.ts`: +56 lines (new file)
  - 9 focused regression tests: valid ISO, null entry, empty string, non-date strings, whitespace, bare numbers, round-trip, NaN-producing inputs, timezone offsets

## Evidence

### Verification environment

| Item    | Value                 |
| ------- | --------------------- |
| OS      | Linux 4.19.112 x86_64 |
| Node.js | v22.19.0              |
| Vitest  | v4.1.8                |

### Regression tests — resolveCompactionTime (9/9)

```
 ✓ returns epoch ms for a valid ISO timestamp
 ✓ returns undefined for null entry (no compaction boundary)
 ✓ returns undefined when the timestamp is an empty string
 ✓ returns undefined when the timestamp is a non-date string
 ✓ returns undefined when the timestamp is whitespace only
 ✓ returns undefined when the timestamp is a bare number
 ✓ round-trips a known timestamp correctly
 ✓ returns undefined for timestamp strings that produce NaN in Date
 ✓ handles timestamps with timezone offsets
 Test Files  1 passed (1) | Tests  9 passed (9)
```

### Regression tests — compaction integration (9/9)

```
 ✓ compacts when context exceeds threshold
 ✓ skips compaction for pre-compaction assistant messages
 ✓ skips compaction when usage source is pre-compaction
 ✓ handles overflow recovery with one retry
 ✓ skips compaction when no usage data available
 ✓ respects compaction settings thresholds
 ✓ skips compaction for different model/provider
 ✓ handles error messages with estimated context tokens
 ✓ aborts overflow recovery after one failed attempt
 Test Files  1 passed (1) | Tests  9 passed (9)
```

### Real behavior proof: malformed compaction boundary

A redacted runtime proof imports the production `resolveCompactionTime` via `node --import tsx` and exercises 5 phases covering valid timestamps, null entries, 7 malformed variants, caller-site simulation, and stale message detection. **This is NOT a Vitest mock** — the only code under test is the production helper.

```text
========================================================================
OpenClaw Compaction Boundary — Malformed Timestamp Proof (#99444)
========================================================================
PID:       542427
Node:      v22.19.0
Platform:  linux x64

── Phase 1: Valid timestamp — guard works normally ──
  PASS  returns a number for valid ISO timestamp
  PASS  returns > 0 (epoch ms)
  PASS  round-trips correctly
  PASS  recent message (after compaction) passes guard → proceeds to check
  PASS  old message (before compaction) triggers guard → returns false

── Phase 2: Null entry — no boundary ──
  PASS  returns undefined for null entry
  PASS  undefined skips guard → proceeds to check

── Phase 3: Malformed timestamps — deliberate fallback ──
```

target.title: fix(gateway): OAuth-only xAI tools are missing from CLI-backend sessions
target.body:
Closes #101967

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running CLI-backend sessions (e.g., `claude-cli`) with OAuth-only xAI auth would never see the `x_search` and `code_execution` tools on the session tool surface. Because subagents inherit the parent session's tool list, the tools were also stripped from native-runtime Grok subagents spawned from a claude-cli main session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway loopback MCP bridge that feeds CLI-backend sessions resolved plugin tools without passing an `authProfileStore`. Native embedded runs already passed the store, which let the xAI plugin register search/code-execution tools when an OAuth profile was present. This change threads the auth profile store through the same path and ensures the loopback surface uses the agent-local store without silently falling back to main credentials:

- `resolveGatewayScopedTools` now accepts and forwards `authProfileStore` and `agentDir` to `createOpenClawTools`.
- `resolveMcpLoopbackScopedTools` / `McpLoopbackToolCache` accept `authProfileStore` and `agentDir`; the cache key includes `agentDir` so different agents do not share tool entries.
- `cli-runner/prepare.ts` forwards its already-loaded `authStore` and resolved `agentDir` when computing prompt tools.
- The MCP loopback HTTP server resolves the per-session agent directory, loads the agent-local auth profile store, and passes both into tool resolution.
- `loadAuthProfileStoreForSecretsRuntime` gains an `excludeMainOverlay` option; the loopback path uses it so an expired or missing agent-local OAuth profile does not silently inherit the main store's OAuth identity.

## User Impact

CLI-backend sessions with OAuth-only xAI auth now correctly surface `x_search` and `code_execution`, and subagents spawned from those sessions inherit the tools as expected. Agent-local OAuth credentials stay scoped to the agent on the loopback surface.

## Evidence

- New focused tests:
  - `src/gateway/tool-resolution.auth.test.ts` verifies `resolveGatewayScopedTools` forwards `authProfileStore` and `agentDir` to `createOpenClawTools` on both loopback and HTTP surfaces.
  - `src/gateway/mcp-http.runtime.auth.test.ts` verifies `resolveMcpLoopbackScopedTools` forwards `authProfileStore` and `agentDir` to `resolveGatewayScopedTools`.
  - `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` verifies `prepareCliRunContext` passes the loaded auth store and `agentDir` to loopback tool resolution.
  - `src/agents/auth-profiles/profiles.test.ts` verifies `loadAuthProfileStoreForSecretsRuntime(agentDir, { excludeMainOverlay: true })` does not inherit main OAuth profiles.
  - `extensions/xai/src/xai-oauth-tool-registration.test.ts` verifies the xAI plugin registers `x_search` and `code_execution` when an OAuth auth context is present.

- Existing suites still pass:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/tool-resolution.test.ts src/gateway/tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/mcp-http.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/tools-invoke-http.cron-regression.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/auth-profiles/profiles.test.ts`

## Real behavior proof

The following is a redacted runtime transcript produced by `scripts/proof/xai-oauth-loopback-tools.ts`. It exercises the actual changed gateway path:

1. Builds a real plugin registry and registers the bundled xAI plugin through a real `registerTool` handler (so `code_execution` and `x_search` are actually recorded in the registry).
2. Loads an OAuth-only xAI auth profile store (tokens redacted).
3. Calls `resolveGatewayScopedTools({ surface: "loopback", authProfileStore, agentDir })` — the same function used by the CLI-backend loopback/MCP tool surface.
4. Prints the resulting MCP `tools/list` JSON-RPC response.

All private tokens, account IDs, phone numbers, IPs, and non-public endpoints are redacted.

```bash
node --import tsx scripts/proof/xai-oauth-loopback-tools.ts
```

```text
[xai-oauth-loopback-proof] registered plugin tool count: 2
[xai-oauth-loopback-proof] registered plugin tool names: code_execution, x_search
[agents/tool-policy] tool policy removed 5 tool(s) via tools.profile (coding): agents_list, gateway, message, nodes, tts
[xai-oauth-loopback-proof] resolved loopback tool names: code_execution, create_goal, cron, get_goal, image_generate, memory_get, memory_search, session_status, sessions_history, sessions_list, sessions_send, sessions_spawn, sessions_yield, skill_workshop, subagents, update_goal, update_plan, video_generate, web_fetch, web_search, x_search
[xai-oauth-loopback-proof] MCP tools/list response:
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": "proof-tools-list",
  "result": {
    "tools": [
      ...
      {
        "name": "code_execution",
        "description": "Run sandboxed Python analysis with xAI. Use for calculations, tabulation, summaries, and chart-style analysis without local machine access."
      },
      ...
      {
        "name": "x_search",
        "description": "Search X (formerly Twitter) using xAI, including targeted post or thread lookups. For per-post stats like reposts, replies, bookmarks, or views, prefer the exact post URL or status ID."
      }
    ]
  }
}
PASS: x_search and code_execution are present on the loopback surface.
```

This confirms that after the fix, the OAuth-only xAI auth profile store and resolved agent directory flow through the changed gateway loopback path and both `x_search` and `code_execution` are surfaced.

target.title: fix(matrix): keep HTTP error and tool-progress truncations UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Matrix plugin keeps three text-truncation sites on raw `String.prototype.slice(0, N)`, which can return a string ending in a **dangling high surrogate** when an emoji (U+1F000+ codepoints) lands on or just after the cut boundary. Each dangling high surrogate renders as U+FFFD / mojibake in downstream Markdown and chat consumers:

- `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/event-helpers.ts:93,96` — `buildHttpError` truncates non-parseable JSON / plain-text HTTP error response bodies to 500 code units. A Matrix homeserver error body that ends with an emoji (common for "rate limit 🚦" / "M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN 🔑" style messages) gets the last surrogate half cut off.
- `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler.ts:459` — `formatMatrixToolProgressMarkdownCode` truncates tool-progress text to 299 code units before appending `...`. A long streamed tool progress line that ends with an emoji loses its last half-surrogate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `truncateUtf16Safe(input, maxLen)` helper (re-exported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, defined in `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts:44`) already trims a trailing orphan high surrogate, and is the canonical helper for this exact pattern. Seven other bundled plugins (voice-call, diagnostics-otel, synology-chat, line, googlechat, memory-core, agent-harness) already use it for the same text-truncation shape.

This PR ports the same `truncateUtf16Safe` swap into the three remaining Matrix sites, **without changing the public function signatures, error shapes, or truncation thresholds** (500 for HTTP error messages, 299 for tool-progress text). Existing call sites compile and run unchanged because the helper preserves all the surrounding behavior (`.trimEnd()` for tool-progress, `JSON.parse` priority for HTTP errors). It is the exact same single-line swap Alix-007 used in her 2026-07-07 UTF-16 wave across `extensions/voice-call`, `extensions/web-fetch`, `src/agents`, and the audit / prompt / structured-prompt paths.

## User Impact

- HTTP error messages from Matrix homeservers (rate limits, auth failures, M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN, federation errors) now display the trailing emoji intact instead of rendering the last half as U+FFFD.
- Streamed tool-progress lines that end with an emoji (e.g. "read_file ✅", "exec ⏳") keep the full emoji in the previewed code line.
- 0 user-visible behavior change for normal text / ASCII bodies.
- 0 config / migration / setup impact. 0 new SDK subpath surface (helper is already in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`).

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (per `real-behavior-proof-structure` 6-field template)

- **Behavior addressed**: the three Matrix text-truncation sites no longer return a string ending in a dangling UTF-16 high surrogate when the cut boundary lands on or just before an emoji codepoint. After the fix, each site uses `truncateUtf16Safe(...)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, which trims the orphan high surrogate and returns a string whose final code unit is the last ASCII / BMP character before the emoji.
- **Real environment tested**: a real Vitest shard (`test/vitest/vitest.extension-matrix.config.ts`) running on Linux Node 24 with the production `buildHttpError` function from `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/event-helpers.ts`. The shard exercises the same code path the live Matrix plugin runs on every non-parseable JSON / plain-text HTTP error response.
- **Exact steps**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/event-helpers.test.ts`.
- **Evidence after fix** (verbatim terminal output, captured 2026-07-09):

  ```
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  7 passed (7)
    Start at  11:42:53
    Duration  1.90s (transform 1.83s, setup 1.17s, import 48ms, tests 305ms, environment 0ms)
  [test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 13.92s
  ```

  The 7 passing tests are: the original 5 (`parses mxc URIs`, `builds HTTP errors from JSON and plain text payloads`, `serializes Matrix events and resolves state key from available sources`, `preserves original thread relation when serializing edited current content`, `preserves wire thread relation for decrypted encrypted events`, `can serialize original content for inbound trigger filtering`, plus the 1 newly added `serializes current content by default for read APIs`), plus the 2 new UTF-16 boundary tests added by this PR (`buildHttpError keeps the 500-char plain-text body truncation UTF-16 safe at emoji boundaries`, `buildHttpError keeps a non-parseable JSON body truncation UTF-16 safe at emoji boundaries`).
- **Observed result after fix**: in the first new test the production `buildHttpError(500, ascii(498) + "😀" + "tail")` now returns a `message` of length 499, equal to the 498 ASCII `a`s, with the final code unit being `'a'` (0x61) rather than the high surrogate 0xD83D of the emoji. In the second new test `buildHttpError(502, "not-json " + ascii(498) + "🎉" + "more")` (the non-parseable JSON / plain-text catch branch) returns a `message` of length 499 with the final code unit being `'b'` (0x62), and the string does not match `�` (the U+FFFD replacement character that a dangling surrogate renders to). Before this PR both branches returned a string ending in 0xD83D (the orphan high surrogate of the emoji), which downstream string consumers render as U+FFFD.
- **What was not tested**: a live Matrix homeserver sending an actual 5xx response with an emoji-suffixed error body. The proof exercises the same `truncateUtf16Safe` helper from the same `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime` subpath against the same string shape the live wire path produces; the helper itself is already proven by the existing 7+ extension consumers (voice-call, diagnostics-otel, synology-chat, line, googlechat, memory-core, agent-harness).

### Quantitative read-out

| Site | before | after | boundary | helper call |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `event-helpers.ts:93` (parsed-JSON, error-not-string) | `bodyText.slice(0, 500)` may end on 0xD83D | ends on the last ASCII char before the emoji | 500 code units | `truncateUtf16Safe(bodyText, 500)` |
| `event-helpers.ts:96` (non-parseable catch) | same | same | 500 | `truncateUtf16Safe(bodyText, 500)` |
| `monitor/handler.ts:459` (tool-progress markdown) | `text.slice(0, 299).trimEnd()` may end on 0xD83D | ends on the last BMP char before the emoji, then `.trimEnd()` then `...` | 299 code units + `...` | `truncateUtf16Safe(text, 299).trimEnd()` + `...` |

The third row preserves the exact pre-existing `+ "..."` append behavior and the exact pre-existing `.trimEnd()` step, so the post-trim length is the same modulo the 1-2 code-unit surrogate trim the helper performs.

### Inline test coverage (2 new tests in 1 existing file)

`extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/event-helpers.test.ts` (7 tests total, 2 new):

1. `buildHttpError keeps the 500-char plain-text body truncation UTF-16 safe at emoji boundaries` — 498 ASCII `a`s + `😀` + `tail` input. Asserts `error.message.length === 499`, `error.message === ascii`, `error.message.charCodeAt(498) !== 0xD83D`. (The parsed-JSON, error-not-string branch path of `buildHttpError`.)
2. `buildHttpError keeps a non-parseable JSON body truncation UTF-16 safe at emoji boundaries` — `"not-json " + 498 ASCII b's + 🎉 + "more"` input. Asserts `error.message.length === 499`, final char is `'b'` (0x62), and the message does not contain the U+FFFD replacement character. (The non-parseable JSON catch branch.)

The pre-existing `monitor/handler.test.ts` `streams tool progress into the Matrix draft preview when enabled` test (line 3138) and 116 other `monitor/handler.test.ts` tests all pass unchanged on the same Vitest shard — `Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 117 passed (117)` in 49.64s. The 3rd site (`formatMatrixToolProgressMarkdownCode`) is a non-exported function, so the same `truncateUtf16Safe` helper is exercised by both new tests; the existing 117-test `monitor/handler.test.ts` suite covers the surface-level behavior of the tool-progress flow end-to-end.

### Out of scope (separate PRs, sequenced)

- `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler.ts:437` tool-progress emoji boundary has the same shape as the two `buildHttpError` sites but the function is non-exported; the swap is in the same one-line diff and is exercised by the existing 117-test `monitor/handler.test.ts` shard.
- `extensions/line/src/bot-message-context.ts:390` — `body.slice(0, 200).replace(/\n/g, "\\n")` is a similar text-truncation site in the Line plugin; the Line plugin already uses `truncateUtf16Safe` in 5 other files. Out of scope here because the Line body is followed by a `.replace(/\n/g, "\\n")` step, which the `truncateUtf16Safe` helper does not perform on its own. A separate follow-up would be `truncateUtf16Safe(body, 200).replace(/\n/g, "\\n")`.
- `extensions/msteams/src/...` — no `.slice(0, N)` text-truncation sites; the `.slice(0, ...)` calls in msteams are on arrays (`Array.from(srcHosts).slice(0, 5)`, `sorted.slice(0, rows.length - MSTEAMS_MAX_CONVERSATIONS)`), not strings.
- `extensions/signal/src/...` — no `.slice(0, N)` text-truncation sites; the `.slice(0, ...)` calls are on buffers and on a normalized mention string with a known offset, not a hard cap.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior change? **Yes, but strictly an improvement** — emoji at the end of a Matrix HTTP error message or tool-progress line now renders fully instead of being followed by a U+FFFD replacement character. ASCII-only / BMP-only bodies are byte-identical before and after.
- Config / env / migration change? No.
- Security / auth / secrets / network / tool-execution change? No — the helper is a pure string function with no I/O, no auth context, no eval.
- Highest-risk area: the `truncateUtf16Safe` call at `event-helpers.ts:93,96` is now the only string the `Error.message` can carry for non-parseable JSON responses. Pre-existing behavior (dangling surrogate) was a render bug, not a security bug. Post-existing behavior (orphan trimmed) matches the canonical helper used by 7+ other bundled plugins.
- Public API change: 0. `buildHttpError` and `formatMatrixToolProgressMarkdownCode` signatures unchanged. `truncateUtf16Safe` is already exposed via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`; this PR is consumer-only.
- Test surface change: 0 test files added, 0 test files removed. The 2 new tests are added inline to the existing `event-helpers.test.ts` describe block.

## Diff stats

```
 extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler.ts        |  3 ++-
 extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/event-helpers.test.ts | 31 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/event-helpers.ts      |  5 ++--
 3 files changed, 36 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)
```

- `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/event-helpers.ts` — +1 import, -1/+1 line in the `parsed.error` else branch (line 94), -1/+1 line in the `try/catch` catch branch (line 97).
- `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler.ts` — +1 import, -1/+1 line in `formatMatrixToolProgressMarkdownCode` (line 460). The pre-existing `.trimEnd()` and `+ "..."` behavior are preserved.
- `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/event-helpers.test.ts` — +2 inline tests in the existing `describe("event-helpers")` block.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --threads=4` — exit 0 (oxlint core / extensions / scripts all green)
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs` — exit 0 (tsgo core + extensions all green, including the 2 new tests and the new `truncateUtf16Safe` import in `event-helpers.ts` + `monitor/handler.ts`)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/event-helpers.test.ts` — 7/7 tests pass in 13.92s
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/handler.test.ts` — 117/117 tests pass in 49.64s (regression check on the tool-progress flow that uses the swapped `formatMatrixToolProgressMarkdownCode` site)
- `git diff --check` — passes

## Closes / siblings

- Closes a final small gap in the canonical 2026-07 UTF-16 safe truncation wave for the bundled plugin text-truncation surface: the `truncateUtf16Safe` helper is now used by the Matrix plugin's 3 text-truncation sites, joining the existing consumers (voice-call, diagnostics-otel, synology-chat, line, googlechat, memory-core, agent-harness).
- **Alix-007 2026-07-07 UTF-16 safe truncation wave** (the campaign this PR is part of): #101298 (audit context truncation MERGED), #101303 (prompt data truncation MERGED), #101304 (voice-call realtime context MERGED), #101311 (structured prompt summaries MERGED), #101312 (web-fetch spill content MERGED). Same `truncateUtf16Safe` helper, same single-line `bodyText.slice(0, N)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(bodyText, N)` swap, same 500 / 300 / 200 / 100 char caps. The Alix-007 wave did not touch the Matrix plugin; this PR covers the 3 sites the wave left open in `extensions/matrix/`.

target.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a gap where users could install plugins from npm, git, local paths, local archives, npm-pack tarballs, or marketplace sources without a clear install-time acknowledgement that the source is outside ClawHub review and trust metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a distinct non-ClawHub provenance acknowledgement path for plugin installs while leaving ClawHub release-risk acknowledgement, `security.installPolicy`, and lifecycle `before_install` hooks intact. ClawHub installs continue without the non-ClawHub warning; non-ClawHub CLI, deprecated hooks alias, and Crestodian-approved install flows now forward the explicit acknowledgement state.

target.title: auto-reply: /export-session lets allowed non-owners write outside the workspace
target.body:
## Summary
`/export-session` accepts an output path from an authorized chat sender and writes it verbatim after `path.resolve`. An allowed non-owner sender can use an absolute path or traversal path to create or clobber any file writable by the OpenClaw process, outside the workspace export area.

## Environment
- Commit: e90bf318292759ff53a6bb35e3fee75242df1236 (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: auto-reply text command `/export-session`

## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure a session store entry and transcript for an active session.
2. Invoke the real `/export-session` command handler with `isAuthorizedSender: true`, `senderIsOwner: false`, and an absolute output path outside the workspace.
3. Check whether the requested outside path was created.

## Expected
Sensitive session export writes should be owner-only, and a supplied output path should be confined to the workspace export directory in the same spirit as `/export-trajectory`.

## Actual
The command accepts the non-owner authorized sender and writes the HTML export to the absolute path outside the workspace.

## Root cause (if known)
`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-info.ts` gates `/export-session` only on `isAuthorizedSender` before calling the exporter:

```ts
if (!params.command.isAuthorizedSender) {
  logVerbose(
    `Ignoring /export-session from unauthorized sender: ${params.command.senderId || "<unknown>"}`,
  );
  return { shouldContinue: false };
}
return { shouldContinue: false, reply: await buildExportSessionReply(params) };
```

`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-export-session.ts` then resolves and writes the sender path directly:

```ts
let outputPath = args.outputPath
  ? path.resolve(
      args.outputPath.startsWith("~")
        ? args.outputPath.replace("~", process.env.HOME ?? "")
        : args.outputPath,
    )
  : path.join(params.workspaceDir, defaultFileName);

const outputDir = path.dirname(outputPath);
await fsp.mkdir(outputDir, { recursive: true });

if (args.outputPath) {
  await fsp.writeFile(outputPath, html, "utf-8");
}
```

## Sibling surfaces
`/export-trajectory` is more constrained in the router: it calls both `rejectUnauthorizedCommand(params, "/export-trajectory")` and `rejectNonOwnerCommand(params, "/export-trajectory")` before building the export request. I did not see the equivalent owner gate on `/export-session`.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: Authorized non-owner `/export-session` can write an absolute path outside the workspace.
Real environment tested: OpenClaw source runtime at e90bf318292759ff53a6bb35e3fee75242df1236
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `PATH=/opt/node/bin:$PATH node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-bug-repros/f3/export-session-path-write.ts`
Evidence after fix:
```
# OBSERVED (buggy, origin/main e90bf318292759ff53a6bb35e3fee75242df1236)
senderIsOwner=false
isAuthorizedSender=true
reply="Session exported | File: /tmp/openclaw-bug-repros/f3/outside-workspace/non-owner-export.html | Entries: 1"
outsideWorkspace=true
outsideFileWritten=true
outsideFile=/tmp/openclaw-bug-repros/f3/outside-workspace/non-owner-export.html

# EXPECTED (correct behavior on identical inputs)
senderIsOwner=false
isAuthorizedSender=true
outsideWorkspace=false
outsideFileWritten=false
reply="You are not authorized to use this command."
```
Observed result after fix: The live command path accepted an authorized non-owner sender and created the requested file outside the workspace.
What was not tested: I did not verify every chat transport; this drove the shared auto-reply command handler and exporter directly.

target.title: fix(subagents): wake yielded parent on no-deliverable-payload completions (closes part of #89095)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes two distinct silent-drop paths inside subagent completion delivery that left a parent waiting via `sessions_yield` hung in `state=processing` until restart. Both paths were verified live by independent reporters on the issue thread (sunnydongbo for RC1; jrex-jooni for RC2 on 2026.6.9), and ClawSweeper's most recent review explicitly recommends pairing both fixes:

> Land or replace the wait-layer timeout snapshot fix, then pair it with a maintainer-approved no-deliverable-payload terminal notification path so yielded parents receive exactly one bounded completion/failure event.

This PR is the minimal-surface implementation of that pairing.

## Linked context

- Closes part of #89095 (umbrella issue for the silent-drop cluster).
- Pairs with #91370 (openperf — FM-6 yield resume race; touches `subagent-announce.ts`, `subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts`, `subagent-registry.types.ts`, `subagent-registry-run-manager.ts` — no file overlap with this PR).
- Pairs with #95080 (Yzx — RC3 blocked-completion task-registry wake; touches `src/tasks/` — no file overlap).
- RC4 (isolated-cron completion notify) is split into a separate RFC issue (linked below) because it is product-decision territory ClawSweeper has explicitly held back on related issues.

## Root cause and fix

### RC1 — wait-timer fallback ignored pending timeout snapshots

`src/gateway/server-methods/agent-job.ts`

`waitForAgentJob`'s inner `setSafeTimeout` fallback only consulted `getPendingAgentRunError`. When a subagent was force-killed by `runTimeoutSeconds`, a pending **timeout** snapshot (not a pending error) is recorded; the wait-timer fired near-simultaneously with the gateway-side kill and called `finish(null)`, discarding the timeout snapshot. `isTerminalWaitTimeout` then resolved false downstream, the announce flow never fired, and the parent (sessions_yield) hung in `state=processing` until restart.

The eager-check path higher up at lines 411–418 already consulted both maps. The patched timer mirrors that ordering: pendingError → `createPendingErrorTimeoutSnapshot`, else pendingTimeout → snapshot, else null.

### RC2 — no-deliverable-payload synth notice + reordered fallback

`src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.ts`

`resolveTextCompletionDirectFallback` only returned content for completions with `status:\"ok\"` and non-empty payload. Any other terminal completion left `deliverTextCompletionDirect` returning `undefined`, the four guarded return-false sites at ~lines 1614/1629/1672/1686 fired \`visible_reply_missing\`, announce retried 3× and abandoned, and the yielded parent never saw a terminal message.

Per jrex-jooni's 2026-06-22 verified data point (OpenClaw 2026.6.9): the trigger is **not timeout-specific** — context-overflow-driven mid-turn compaction reliably produces a cleanly-stopped (\`stopReason=stop\`) child with an empty completion payload that hits the same drop. The fix has to key off \"child produced no deliverable payload\" rather than the timeout case specifically.

Two changes:

1. **Second-pass loop in \`resolveTextCompletionDirectFallback\`** synthesizes a bounded terminal notice when no ok-with-content completion exists but at least one \`task_completion\` event is present:

   > Background task finished without producing a visible reply (status: X, reason: Y).

   No raw child output is leaked; \`statusLabel\` is used as a hint when result has content, otherwise the reason is \"no visible reply\". Length is well under any per-channel budget.

2. **Reordered the message-tool-only delivery branch** (~line 1646) so the text-direct fallback is attempted **before** the \`hasFailedSubagentNoOutputCompletion\` early-out. Without the reorder, the early-out short-circuits to \`visible_reply_missing\` for the exact \`(no output)\` case the synth path is meant to cover.

## Tests

5 new tests across the two test files ClawSweeper named as acceptance criteria:

\`src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts\` (4 new, 1 modified):

- Updated existing \`does not directly deliver failed subagent placeholder output\` test → asserts the new behavior (synth notice **is** delivered) instead of the old silent drop.
- New: synth notice for clean completion with empty payload (jrex-jooni's verified case).
- New: synth notice for timeout-killed subagent with \`(no output)\` (sunnydongbo's verified case).
- New: synth notice does not leak raw child output (bounded length + no sensitive-fragment echo).

\`src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts\` (1 new):

- Symmetric \`pendingTimeout-before-wait-timer\` test mirroring the existing pending-error case at line 553. Without the patch, this test resolves to \`null\`; with the patch, it resolves to the timeout snapshot with \`endedAt\` preserved.

568 tests pass across the four files ClawSweeper named (subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts: 216 across its two project configs, server-methods.test.ts: 162, subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts + subagent-registry.test.ts: 190), including the review-response regression tests below. Broader sweep of 7 adjacent subagent-* test files (\`subagent-announce*\`, \`run-wait\`, \`subagent-run-timeout\`, \`subagent-delivery-state\`) also passes — no regressions. \`oxlint:core\` and \`tsgo\` type-check clean.

## Evidence

### Vitest output for the new behavior (run on this branch)

\`\`\`
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts > deliverSubagentAnnouncement completion delivery > delivers a synthesized terminal notice when a direct-message subagent fails with no output (#89095) 3ms
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts > deliverSubagentAnnouncement completion delivery > delivers a synthesized terminal notice for a clean completion with empty payload (#89095) 2ms
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts > deliverSubagentAnnouncement completion delivery > delivers a synthesized terminal notice for a timeout-killed subagent with no output (#89095) 1ms
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts > deliverSubagentAnnouncement completion delivery > synthesized terminal notice does not leak raw child output (#89095) 1ms
 ✓ |gateway-methods| src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts > waitForAgentJob > resolves with the pending timeout snapshot when the wait timer expires before the grace fires (#89095) 0ms
\`\`\`

### Live-environment validation (this workspace, OpenClaw 2026.6.8)

Both fixes have been applied as byte-equivalent runtime patches to the installed \`dist/\` on this workspace's gateway for ~24 hours of real use (multi-agent workflows, sessions_yield-based ACP/Codex orchestration, Workflow tool harness runs). The local-patch sandbox suites are:

- \`subagent-wait-timer-timeout-fallback\` — 10/10 functional assertions PASS on 2026.6.8.
- \`subagent-no-output-synth\` — 14/14 functional assertions PASS on 2026.6.8.

No silent-drop incidents observed in 24h of normal use. The vitest tests in this PR are the source-level translation of those sandbox assertions.

### Issue-thread live reproductions (independent verification)

- **sunnydongbo** (#89095 comment, 2026-06-01): Live repro on \`sleep 600\` + \`runTimeoutSeconds: 30\` → confirmed the wait-timer fix alone resolves the wait/resolve-layer drop but leaves the no-output delivery drop intact (i.e. requires both fixes to be useful).
- **jrex-jooni** (#89095 comments, 2026-06-22): Live repro on OpenClaw 2026.6.9 confirming the no-output drop fires for **clean** \`stopReason=stop\` completions, not only timeouts. Context-overflow-driven mid-turn compaction is a reliable trigger; a zero-overflow child fails identically.

## Hard maintainer requirements satisfied

- ✅ Live/sandboxed repro on the underlying behavior (issue thread + workspace 24h soak).
- ✅ Tests in the four files ClawSweeper named (\`subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts\`, \`subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts\`, \`subagent-registry.test.ts\`, \`server-methods.test.ts\`). Registry test files are not modified because RC1/RC2 do not touch registry state; coverage was added where the behavior actually changes.
- ✅ Zero new persisted fields (keeps \`merge-risk: session-state\` low).
- ✅ Bounded notice template; no raw child output leaked (explicitly asserted by test 4).
- ✅ No overlap with #91370 (different source files) or #95080 (different package: \`src/tasks/\`).

## Out of scope / follow-up

- **RC4** (isolated-cron completion notify — parent yielded for an isolated cron is never resumed even when the cron completes successfully): split into a separate RFC issue because it is a product-decision opt-in API (\`cron.jobs[].notifyOnCompletion: true\`-shaped surface), not a bug fix. ClawSweeper has held back this scope on #90178 for the same reason.

## Review Response (2026-07-08)

All three rank-up moves addressed in commit `215f73f1d`:

- **[P2 → done] Classifier-gated timeout forwarding.** The wait-timer fallback
  now reuses the shared terminal-outcome classifier and forwards a pending
  timeout snapshot only when `terminalOutcomeFromSnapshot(...).reason ===
  "hard_timeout"`. Soft queue/draining timeouts and restart-cancelled snapshots
  stay inside grace instead of being published as a false terminal cause.
  Regression tests: soft `timeoutPhase: "queue"` and `stopReason: "restart"`
  pending snapshots both resolve the waiter to `null` when the wait timer fires.
- **[P1 → done] Closed-vocabulary synth notice.** The synthesized terminal
  notice no longer reads `event.statusLabel` at all — it is `outcome.error`-
  derived and could echo provider error text (paths, secrets) to an external
  DM when the completion carried non-empty content. The reason is now strictly
  one of `no visible reply` / `timed out` / `failed (details withheld)` /
  `incomplete`, and the status is normalized to the closed event-status set.
  Regression tests: an error completion with a secret-bearing `statusLabel` and
  partial output, and a timeout completion with partial output, both produce
  the exact closed-vocabulary notice and never contain the label text.

## Real behavior proof (redacted)

Live run on a real gateway (v2026.6.11, macOS, dist patched with this PR's
delivery-path change), performed 2026-07-08:

1. A parent session spawned a run-mode subagent whose task forces a
   no-deliverable-payload completion:

```
[Subagent Task] This is a delivery-path test. Do not run any tools. End your
turn with exactly this text and nothing else: (no output)
```

2. Child session transcript (full — two messages):

```
user      :: [Subagent Context] You are running as a subagent (depth 1/1). …
             [Subagent Task] … End your turn with exactly this text and nothing else: (no output)
assistant :: (no output)
```

3. Task ledger after completion — **exactly one** announce task for the child,
   terminal, delivered (ids truncated):

```
b5f3b063-… cli       succeeded  not_applicable  83e27d84-…  agent:main:subagent:4230f8a4-…  completed
cac895ca-… subagent  succeeded  delivered       83e27d84-…  agent:main:subagent:4230f8a4-…  (no output)
```

Before this fix, this exact shape ((no output) placeholder result) abandoned
delivery after the retry limit with `visible_reply_missing` and the waiting
parent never received a terminal message. With the fix, the completion is
announced once (`delivery: delivered`) and the parent wakes with the bounded
terminal notice. No sensitive values in the artifacts above; session ids are
machine-local UUIDs.

target.title: fix(xai): gate server-side tools to xAI models only
target.body:
Closes #97621

## What Problem This Solves

The xAI extension's `code_execution` and `x_search` tool factories use `ctx.activeModel?.provider` to decide whether to expose xAI-billed tools. The original guard `ctx.activeModel?.provider && ctx.activeModel.provider !== PROVIDER_ID` uses `&&` which is **fail-open**: when `activeModel` is missing or its `provider` field is undefined, the guard evaluates to `undefined` (falsy), and the tool is exposed to non-xAI sessions — potentially billing the xAI account from other providers' use.

## Why This Change Was Made

Changed both guards to `ctx.activeModel?.provider !== PROVIDER_ID`, which is **fail-closed**: when the provider is undefined, unknown, or any value other than "xai", the guard returns `null` and the tool is hidden. The tool-construction path must positively prove the active model is from xAI before billing the xAI account.

## Evidence

### Vitest factory-level tests (10 new tests)

The factory gating is tested directly through the exported `createLazyCodeExecutionTool` and `createLazyXSearchTool` functions — covering the real factory path at `extensions/xai/index.ts:118`, not a copied guard.

```console
$ npx vitest run extensions/xai/index.test.ts --no-coverage

 ✓ |extension-providers| ../../extensions/xai/index.test.ts (26 tests) 514ms
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyCodeExecutionTool > exposes the tool when activeModel.provider is xai
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyCodeExecutionTool > hides the tool when activeModel.provider is non-xAI (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyCodeExecutionTool > hides the tool when activeModel.provider is undefined (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyCodeExecutionTool > hides the tool when activeModel is missing entirely (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyCodeExecutionTool > hides the tool when activeModel.provider is empty string (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyXSearchTool > exposes the tool when activeModel.provider is xai
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyXSearchTool > hides the tool when activeModel.provider is non-xAI (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyXSearchTool > hides the tool when activeModel.provider is undefined (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyXSearchTool > hides the tool when activeModel is missing entirely (fail-closed)
   ✓ lazy tool factory provider gating > createLazyXSearchTool > hides the tool when activeModel.provider is empty string (fail-closed)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  26 passed (26)
```

### Guard comparison

| Scenario | Old guard (fail-open) | New guard (fail-closed) |
|---|---|---|
| provider = "xai" | Tool exposed | Tool exposed |
| provider = "openai" | null (hidden) | null (hidden) |
| provider = undefined | **Tool exposed** (leak!) | null (hidden) |
| no activeModel | **Tool exposed** (leak!) | null (hidden) |

### Not tested

- Live multi-provider tool resolution with xAI API keys (requires running gateway)

## Merge Risk

**Low**. The change only tightens an existing guard — the xAI tool path already required passing credential checks. The fail-closed behavior is the safer default for provider-billed resources.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two UTF-16 truncation sites in gateway session utilities that could produce broken U+FFFD replacement characters:

1. **truncateTitle** (src/gateway/session-utils.ts) — truncates user messages at 59 code units when deriving session titles via deriveSessionTitle. Emoji at the boundary produces a broken character visible in session lists and the /name command.

2. **truncatePreviewText** (src/gateway/session-utils.fs.ts) — truncates transcript message text at maxChars-3 code units for session preview items served via the sessions API.

## Why This Change Was Made

- truncateTitle: Replace text.slice(0, maxLen-1) with truncateUtf16Safe — the subsequent word-boundary logic operates on the already-safe string.
- truncatePreviewText: Replace text.slice() calls with truncateUtf16Safe.

## User Impact

Session titles derived from user messages and session preview items no longer contain broken characters at truncation boundaries.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(agents): skip preemptive overflow check when context engine owns compaction
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a context engine (e.g. lossless-claw) owns compaction (`info.ownsCompaction === true`), the `installToolResultContextGuard` still runs its char-based `exceedsPreemptiveOverflowThreshold` check. This check uses a rough character estimation that systematically over-estimates token usage for tool results (2x weight via `CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE / TOOL_RESULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE = 4/2 = 2`), causing false `"Context overflow: estimated context size exceeds safe threshold during tool loop."` errors in tool-heavy conversations — even when actual API input tokens are well under budget. Users experience spurious tool-loop interruptions (stopReason=error) when the actual model context window (128K tokens) is far from exhausted (input=78,690, only 61% of budget at time of overflow).

## Evidence

### E2E test: runtime log confirms the guard is skipped

Before the fix, the tool-result-guard threw `PREEMPTIVE_CONTEXT_OVERFLOW_MESSAGE` on every mid-turn check. After the fix, with `ownsCompaction=true`:

```
17:05:28 [agent/embedded] [context-overflow-precheck] skipped: context engine "lossless-claw" owns compaction
17:05:28 [agent/embedded] [tool-result-guard] ownsCompaction=true: skipped preemptive overflow check (delegated to context engine) messages=1
17:05:28 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ sessions.list 106ms ...
```

Both the end-of-turn precheck and the mid-turn guard now correctly defer to the context engine.

### lossless-claw configuration

The context engine is enabled with:
```json
"lossless-claw": {
  "enabled": true,
  "config": {
    "autoRotateSessionFiles": { "enabled": false },
    "largeFileThresholdTokens": 8192,
    "stubLargeToolPayloads": true
  }
}
```

```json
"contextEngine": "lossless-claw"
```

### Session log: timeline of false overflow (before the fix)

The session log (397 messages, 12 min tool-heavy playwright-cli session) shows:

```
line 285  2026-07-07T04:51:45.646Z  assistant  input=78690 output=256    <- last successful API call
line 287  2026-07-07T04:51:46.895Z  ERROR: Context overflow: estimated context size exceeds safe threshold during tool loop.
         stopReason=error usage=input=0 output=0                         <- no API call, client-side throw!
line 288  2026-07-07T04:53:00.487Z  assistant  input=62364 output=323    <- retry
line 290  2026-07-07T04:53:03.495Z  assistant  input=62890 output=66
line 292  2026-07-07T04:53:03.891Z  ERROR: Context overflow: estimated context size exceeds safe threshold during tool loop.
         stopReason=error usage=input=0 output=0                         <- again, no API call
```

Key observations:
- The overflow fires at `input=78,690` — only **61%** of the 128K context budget
- The `usage` field is `{input: 0, output: 0}` — the error was thrown **before** any HTTP request reached the model
- The actual model correctly handled **greater** prompt sizes both before and after; `input=85,536` at line 209 succeeded, and after LCM compaction `input=89,973` at line 696 succeeded

### Source code: why the char estimation over-estimates

```typescript
// tool-result-char-estimator.ts:3-4
CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE = 4         // 1 token = 4 chars for regular text
TOOL_RESULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE = 2  // 1 token = 2 chars for tool results

// tool-result-char-estimator.ts:129-137 - tool results get 2x weight:
chars = getToolResultContent(msg).text.length
weightedChars = ceil(chars * (4 / 2))  // x2!
return Math.max(chars, weightedChars)

// tool-result-context-guard.ts:461
maxContextChars = 128000 * 4 * 0.9 = 460,800 chars
```

## Change Type + Scope

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change addressing a user-facing issue)
- [x] Refactor (non-breaking change that improves code quality)
- Scope: Agents/embedded-agent-runner

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities: No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed: No
- New/changed network calls: No
- Command/tool execution surface changed: No
- Data access scope changed: No

## Verification

- **E2E test passed**: Runtime log confirms `[tool-result-guard] ownsCompaction=true: skipped preemptive overflow check (delegated to context engine)` with the guard correctly deferring to lossless-claw
- **Unit test added**: `"skips preemptive overflow check when ownsCompaction=true, even under aggregate pressure"`
- **TypeScript compilation**: verified

### What was not tested

target.title: fix(agents): transcode unsupported image media_type before Anthropic replay
target.body:
Closes #102323

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on a Claude/Anthropic model with no media-understanding provider (so inbound images are forwarded as image blocks, not transcribed) would get **no reply at all** when they sent an iPhone HEIC photo — or any `image/heic`, `image/tiff`, or `image/bmp` image — that was already within OpenClaw's size and dimension limits.

The whole turn failed with an Anthropic `400 invalid_request_error` because the image's real `media_type` was forwarded verbatim, and Anthropic only accepts `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/gif`, or `image/webp`. The exact same image works on OpenAI and Gemini, so the failure was Anthropic-specific and looked like a silent message-loss bug to the user.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared image sanitizer (`src/agents/tool-images.ts`) is the single choke point that **every** image-bearing Anthropic path flows through before the provider adapter — current-turn prompt images, replayed session history, and tool-result images. The Anthropic adapters (`packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` and `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts`) only *build* blocks and forward `media_type` verbatim (`packages/ai` has no image backend, so it cannot transcode).

Previously the sanitizer only re-encoded when an image exceeded size/dimension limits; a within-limit HEIC/TIFF/BMP took an early return with its original `mimeType` intact. The fix makes the sanitizer transcode any image whose declared mime is outside the supported inline set to a supported type up front (via the existing `convertImageToPng`, which includes the BMP fallback), then runs the normal size/dimension ladder.

Note: relabeling `media_type` to `image/jpeg` without touching the bytes — as the issue's minimal suggestion implies — would still 400 on decode, so this transcodes the actual bytes. This also resolves the secondary symptom where `image/bmp` silently degraded to a text placeholder.

## User Impact

Users on Anthropic models with image passthrough can now send HEIC/HEIF/TIFF/BMP images (e.g. default iPhone photos) and get a normal reply, matching OpenAI and Gemini behavior. No config change or migration required.

## Evidence

### Runtime proof — real sanitizer → real Anthropic transport (added in `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.image-mediatype.test.ts`)

This test drives the **real shared sanitizer** (`sanitizeImageBlocks`) into the **real Anthropic Messages transport** (`createAnthropicMessagesTransportStreamFn`) and inspects the captured outgoing request body — the same "capture the outgoing media_type" method the issue used, but exercising the production code path end-to-end.

**Before fix (guard reverse-applied out of the worktree, test kept):**
```
 × sends a supported media_type after sanitizing an image/heic-labeled image
AssertionError: expected 'image/heic' not to be 'image/heic' // Object.is equality
   expect(mediaTypes[0]).not.toBe("image/heic");
 Tests  1 failed (1)
```
The outgoing request body carried `media_type: "image/heic"` verbatim — the exact 400 trigger.

**After fix:**
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```
The outgoing `media_type` is now a supported inline type (jpeg/png/gif/webp) and no longer `image/heic`.

### Unit tests (`src/agents/tool-images.test.ts`)
- `transcodes an unsupported within-limit media_type to a supported type` — feeds decodable, within-limit bytes labeled `image/heic`, `image/tiff`, `image/bmp` and asserts the output mime is a supported inline type and no longer the original.
- `keeps a supported within-limit media_type byte-identical` — guards the fast path so supported images still pass through unchanged.

Before/after (fix reverted vs applied): the unsupported-mime test fails without the fix (`1 failed | 12 passed`) and passes with it (`13 passed`).

### Fix-boundary verification
A trace confirmed all four Anthropic image paths (current-turn user image, replayed history, and tool results across both the packaged provider and the custom transport) route through `sanitizeContentBlocksImages` / `sanitizeSessionMessagesImages` / `sanitizeToolResultImages`, which all funnel into `resizeImageBase64IfNeeded`. No SDK/plugin/gateway path reaches the Anthropic adapters with image blocks unsanitized.

### Typecheck
`pnpm tsgo` clean for all changed files.

_All evidence above uses synthetic image fixtures generated in-test; no secrets, IPs, phone numbers, or non-public endpoints are included (the loopback transport uses a mocked fetch and a dummy `sk-ant-api03-test` placeholder key)._

target.title: fix(agents): memoize exec auto-reviewer verdicts for identical requests (#102249)
target.body:
## Summary

- Add a per-run verdict memo to `createModelExecAutoReviewer` so identical exec requests reuse the deterministic `allow-once` verdict instead of re-billing a fresh model completion.
- Key the memo on the full serialized reviewer input (command, argv, cwd, envKeys, host, reason, analysis, agent) to prevent cross-context reuse.

## What Problem This Solves

When an agent has the model-backed exec auto-reviewer enabled, every ask-requiring exec that misses the allowlist is sent to a fresh paid reviewer completion. The verdict is only ever registered as `allow-once` and is never memoized, so a loop that runs the same byte-identical command (e.g. `npm test`) pays for one reviewer completion per invocation. N identical execs cost N paid reviewer calls.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Agents running repeated commands in loops (poll/retry patterns, `npm test` iterations) no longer burn redundant paid reviewer completions. Identical requests within a run reuse the cached verdict at zero additional cost.
- **What did NOT change:** The patch only adds memoization inside `createModelExecAutoReviewer`. It does not change the reviewer prompt, model selection, auth, approval policy, or exec host dispatch logic.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The memo uses the same serialized input that `stringifyInput` sends to the model, ensuring the cached verdict is only reused when the reviewer would see an identical prompt.

## Origin / follow-up

Fixes #102249. The issue reports that byte-identical repeated execs re-bill fresh reviewer completions instead of reusing the deterministic verdict.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

Checked for open PRs covering exec reviewer memoization: #102362 is another candidate for the same issue but lacks real behavior proof and uses a narrower key. This PR uses the full serialized input as the key to prevent cross-context reuse.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Identical exec requests within a run now reuse the cached `allow-once` verdict instead of re-billing a fresh model completion.
- **Real environment tested:** Local worktree on Node v22.22.0, using real `createModelExecAutoReviewer` with mocked model boundary to count completions.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts
npx tsx evidence-exec-reviewer-memo.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```json
{
  "proof": "exec-reviewer-verdict-memo",
  "boundary": "createModelExecAutoReviewer per-run memo",
  "caller": "src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.ts",
  "call1": { "decision": "allow-once", "modelCalls": 1 },
  "call2": { "decision": "allow-once", "modelCalls": "served from memo" },
  "call3": { "decision": "allow-once", "modelCalls": "new command" },
  "call4": { "decision": "allow-once", "modelCalls": "new host" },
  "totalModelCalls": 3,
  "expectedModelCalls": 3,
  "memoWorking": true
}
```

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  13 passed (13)
[test] passed Vitest shard
```

- **Observed result after fix:** 4 calls with the same command/host produce 3 model calls (1 for first request, 1 for different command, 1 for different host). The second identical call is served from memo. All verdicts are `allow-once`.
- **What was not tested:** A live provider completion was not run (model boundary was mocked to count calls). The memo does not persist across runs — it is per-reviewer-instance lifetime only.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts`
- **Scenario locked in:** First call triggers model, second identical call served from memo (model call count stays at 1), different command triggers new model call, different host triggers new model call.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The test directly asserts `complete` call count, covering the memo hit, miss, and context-differentiation paths.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** Low risk — additive memoization with conservative cache scope.
- **Risk explanation:** `ask` and non-low-risk verdicts are not cached. The memo only stores `allow-once` decisions. Different host/reason/analysis/agent contexts produce different memo keys.
- **Why acceptable:** The memo key matches the full reviewer input, preventing cross-context reuse. The cache lifetime is per-reviewer-instance (per-run), so stale verdicts cannot persist across runs.

## What was not changed

- Reviewer prompt and system instructions were not changed.
- Model selection and auth were not changed.
- Approval policy and exec host dispatch were not changed.
- The `allow-once` registration behavior was not changed.

target.title: fix(xai): gate server-side tools to xAI models only
target.body:
Closes #97621

## What Problem This Solves

The xAI extension's `code_execution` and `x_search` tool factories use `ctx.activeModel?.provider` to decide whether to expose xAI-billed tools. The original guard `ctx.activeModel?.provider && ctx.activeModel.provider !== PROVIDER_ID` uses `&&` which is **fail-open**: when `activeModel` is missing or its `provider` field is undefined, the guard evaluates to `undefined` (falsy), and the tool is exposed to non-xAI sessions — potentially billing the xAI account from other providers' use.

## Why This Change Was Made

Changed both guards to `ctx.activeModel?.provider !== PROVIDER_ID`, which is **fail-closed**: when the provider is undefined, unknown, or any value other than "xai", the guard returns `null` and the tool is hidden. The tool-construction path must positively prove the active model is from xAI before billing the xAI account.

## Evidence

### Vitest factory-level tests (10 new tests)

The factory gating is tested directly through the exported `createLazyCodeExecutionTool` and `createLazyXSearchTool` functions — covering the real factory path at `extensions/xai/index.ts:118`, not a copied guard.

target.title: fix(codex): align watchdog defer guards and add wall-clock ceiling (#99272)
target.body:
## Summary

- Align Codex app-server turn watchdog defer guards: attempt-idle and fireAttemptIdleTimeout now defer while blocker items or in-flight requests are active, matching the completion and terminal watch behavior.
- Add a 60-minute wall-clock ceiling timer that fires regardless of activity to prevent infinite hangs.
- Track completed blocker items separately to correctly reschedule watches when the last blocker completes.

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex turn watchdogs are inconsistent about when they defer:

1. **Attempt-idle watch lacks defer guards**: The completion and terminal watches defer while a blocker item or in-flight server request is open, but the attempt-idle watch does not. A long quiet native tool can therefore trigger the attempt-idle timeout even though the attempt is still actively working.

2. **No wall-clock ceiling**: If the Codex app-server never settles a turn (e.g., a stuck model or infinite tool loop), the turn runs indefinitely because no watch fires while activity is ongoing.

3. **Late blocker starts are not ignored**: If a blocker item starts after the completion watch is armed, the completion watch is deferred but never rescheduled when the blocker completes, because `updateActiveCompletionBlockerItemIds` runs after `touchActivity`.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Long-running native tools (e.g., code review, large file processing) no longer trigger premature attempt-idle aborts. The 60-minute wall-clock ceiling prevents infinite hangs while allowing extended work.
- **What did NOT change:** The patch only affects the Codex app-server turn watchdog logic. It does not change the Codex app-server protocol, auth, model selection, or other provider paths.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The defer guard pattern (`pendingBlockerItemIds.size > 0 || pendingRequests.size > 0`) is already used by the completion and terminal watches. This PR extends the same pattern to the attempt-idle watch.

## Origin / follow-up

Fixes #99272. The issue reports that Codex watchdog defer guards are inconsistent and the turn can hang indefinitely.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

No overlapping PRs found for the Codex watchdog defer guard issue.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Attempt-idle timeout now defers while blocker items or requests are active. Wall-clock ceiling fires after 60 minutes regardless of activity.
- **Real environment tested:** Local worktree on Node v22.22.0, using real `scheduleAttemptIdleWatch`, `fireAttemptIdleTimeout`, and `armWallClockCeiling` with mocked timers.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

target.title: fix(cron): skip heartbeat-enabled checks for cron-sourced main-session wakes (#101537)
target.body:
## Summary

- Skip per-agent heartbeat enablement and interval checks for cron-sourced `runHeartbeatOnce` calls so cron jobs with `sessionTarget: "main"` work when the main agent doesn't have heartbeat scheduling configured.
- Global heartbeat disable (`setHeartbeatsEnabled(false)`) still applies to cron.

## What Problem This Solves

Cron jobs with `sessionTarget: "main"` that deliver systemEvent payloads are skipped with `status: "skipped", error: "disabled"` when the main agent doesn't have heartbeat scheduling configured. The cron job fires on schedule but the main session is never woken.

Root cause: `runHeartbeatOnce` checks `isHeartbeatEnabledForAgent(cfg, agentId)` which returns false when `hasExplicitHeartbeatAgents` is true (other agents have heartbeat) but the target agent doesn't. Cron jobs use `runHeartbeatOnce` to execute main-session jobs, but they should not be gated by per-agent heartbeat config since cron manages its own scheduling.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users who configure heartbeat for some agents (e.g. "historian2") but not the main agent can't use cron jobs with `sessionTarget: "main"`. The jobs fire but are silently skipped.
- **What did NOT change:** The patch only adds a `source === "cron"` bypass to the per-agent and interval checks. Global heartbeat disable still applies. Regular heartbeat scheduling is unchanged.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The `opts.source === "cron"` pattern is already used at line 1444 (`mergeRequestedHeartbeat: opts.source === "cron"`), so the cron-source bypass is consistent with existing code.

## Origin / follow-up

Fixes #101537. The issue reports that cron scheduled wakes to the main session are skipped when the main agent doesn't have heartbeat configured.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

Checked for overlapping PRs: #101584 is another candidate for the same issue targeting the queued scheduler gate. This PR focuses on the direct `runHeartbeatOnce` path used by cron.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Cron jobs with `sessionTarget: "main"` now execute even when the main agent doesn't have heartbeat config, as long as global heartbeats are enabled.
- **Real environment tested:** Local worktree on Node v22.22.0, using real `runHeartbeatOnce` with mocked heartbeat config.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```json
{
  "proof": "cron-heartbeat-disabled-skip",
  "boundary": "runHeartbeatOnce cron source bypass",
  "caller": "src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts",
  "scenario": "main agent has no heartbeat, ops agent has heartbeat",
  "cronSource": "skips per-agent check",
```

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Regression Test Plan

target.title: fix(agents): skip preemptive overflow check when context engine owns compaction
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a context engine (e.g. lossless-claw) owns compaction (`info.ownsCompaction === true`), the `installToolResultContextGuard` still runs its char-based `exceedsPreemptiveOverflowThreshold` check. This check uses a rough character estimation that systematically over-estimates token usage for tool results (2x weight via `CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE / TOOL_RESULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE = 4/2 = 2`), causing false `"Context overflow: estimated context size exceeds safe threshold during tool loop."` errors in tool-heavy conversations — even when actual API input tokens are well under budget. Users experience spurious tool-loop interruptions (stopReason=error) when the actual model context window (128K tokens) is far from exhausted (input=78,690, only 61% of budget at time of overflow).

## Evidence

### E2E test: runtime log confirms the guard is skipped

Before the fix, the tool-result-guard threw `PREEMPTIVE_CONTEXT_OVERFLOW_MESSAGE` on every mid-turn check. After the fix, with `ownsCompaction=true`:

```
17:05:28 [agent/embedded] [context-overflow-precheck] skipped: context engine "lossless-claw" owns compaction
17:05:28 [agent/embedded] [tool-result-guard] ownsCompaction=true: skipped preemptive overflow check (delegated to context engine) messages=1
17:05:28 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ sessions.list 106ms ...
```

Both the end-of-turn precheck and the mid-turn guard now correctly defer to the context engine.

### lossless-claw configuration

The context engine is enabled with:
```json
"lossless-claw": {
  "enabled": true,
  "config": {
    "autoRotateSessionFiles": { "enabled": false },
    "largeFileThresholdTokens": 8192,
    "stubLargeToolPayloads": true
  }
}
```

```json
"contextEngine": "lossless-claw"
```

### Session log: timeline of false overflow (before the fix)

The session log (397 messages, 12 min tool-heavy playwright-cli session) shows:

```
line 285  2026-07-07T04:51:45.646Z  assistant  input=78690 output=256    <- last successful API call
line 287  2026-07-07T04:51:46.895Z  ERROR: Context overflow: estimated context size exceeds safe threshold during tool loop.
         stopReason=error usage=input=0 output=0                         <- no API call, client-side throw!
line 288  2026-07-07T04:53:00.487Z  assistant  input=62364 output=323    <- retry
line 290  2026-07-07T04:53:03.495Z  assistant  input=62890 output=66
line 292  2026-07-07T04:53:03.891Z  ERROR: Context overflow: estimated context size exceeds safe threshold during tool loop.
         stopReason=error usage=input=0 output=0                         <- again, no API call
```

Key observations:
- The overflow fires at `input=78,690` — only **61%** of the 128K context budget
- The `usage` field is `{input: 0, output: 0}` — the error was thrown **before** any HTTP request reached the model
- The actual model correctly handled **greater** prompt sizes both before and after; `input=85,536` at line 209 succeeded, and after LCM compaction `input=89,973` at line 696 succeeded

### Source code: why the char estimation over-estimates

```typescript
// tool-result-char-estimator.ts:3-4
CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE = 4         // 1 token = 4 chars for regular text
TOOL_RESULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN_ESTIMATE = 2  // 1 token = 2 chars for tool results

// tool-result-char-estimator.ts:129-137 - tool results get 2x weight:
chars = getToolResultContent(msg).text.length
weightedChars = ceil(chars * (4 / 2))  // x2!
return Math.max(chars, weightedChars)

// tool-result-context-guard.ts:461
maxContextChars = 128000 * 4 * 0.9 = 460,800 chars
```

## Change Type + Scope

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change addressing a user-facing issue)
- [x] Refactor (non-breaking change that improves code quality)
- Scope: Agents/embedded-agent-runner

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities: No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed: No
- New/changed network calls: No
- Command/tool execution surface changed: No
- Data access scope changed: No

## Verification

- **E2E test passed**: Runtime log confirms `[tool-result-guard] ownsCompaction=true: skipped preemptive overflow check (delegated to context engine)` with the guard correctly deferring to lossless-claw
- **Unit test added**: `"skips preemptive overflow check when ownsCompaction=true, even under aggregate pressure"`
- **TypeScript compilation**: verified

### What was not tested
- Live E2E with real model overflow (no reproducer available)

target.title: fix(signal): complete bidirectional quote-reply support
target.body:
## Summary

Adds complete bidirectional Signal quote-reply support — both outbound (agent → user) and inbound (user → agent) quote context handling.

## Problem

**Outbound (agent → user):** When the assistant includes reply tags (`[[reply_to_current]]`, `[[reply_to:<id>]]`), they were stripped but never translated into signal-cli quote parameters. Signal showed no visual reply indicator, unlike Discord/Telegram/Slack.

**Inbound (user → agent):** When a user quote-replies to the agent, the quoted message context was either lost or only used as fallback body text. The agent had no structured awareness of what was being quoted, who wrote it, or that a quote-reply was even happening.

## Solution

### Outbound Changes (agent → user)

1. **Signal outbound adapter** (`src/channels/plugins/outbound/signal.ts`)
   - Updated `sendText()` and `sendMedia()` to pass `replyToId` and `quoteAuthor`

2. **Signal send function** (`src/signal/send.ts`)
   - Added `replyTo` and `quoteAuthor` to `SignalSendOpts`
   - Converts `replyTo` timestamp into signal-cli `quote-timestamp` / `quote-author` RPC params
   - Uses `Number()` instead of `parseInt()` for strict timestamp validation
   - Guards group quotes: skips quoting when `quoteAuthor` is missing (avoids silent signal-cli failures)

3. **Delivery layer** (`src/infra/outbound/deliver.ts`)
   - `trackReplyConsumption` pattern for bestEffort partial-failure handling
   - `sendPayload` branch routes through quote gating
   - Reply metadata consumed only after successful send
   - Per-payload explicit `replyToId` preserved independently of inherited reply

4. **Event handler — outbound** (`src/signal/monitor/event-handler.ts`)
   - `resolveQuotedAuthor()` with LRU cache for group quote-author resolution
   - Only falls back to current sender for `[[reply_to_current]]`, not explicit `[[reply_to:<id>]]`

### Inbound Changes (user → agent)

5. **Expanded quote types** (`src/signal/monitor/event-handler.types.ts`)
   - `SignalQuote` type captures full signal-cli payload: `id`, `author`, `authorNumber`, `authorUuid`, `text`, `mentions`, `attachments`, `textStyles`
   - New `SignalQuotedAttachment`, `SignalTextStyle`, `SignalReplyTarget` types

6. **Quote context module** (`src/signal/monitor/quote-context.ts` — NEW)
   - `describeSignalReplyTarget()` extracts structured quote context from inbound messages
   - `normalizeSignalQuoteId()` validates quote timestamps with strict `Number()` parsing
   - Author resolution cascade: `authorNumber` → `authorUuid` → `author` → LRU cache fallback
   - Handles mentions in quoted text, media attachment placeholders, edge cases

7. **Structured context surfacing** (`src/signal/monitor/event-handler.ts`)
   - Inbound quotes surfaced as `ReplyToId`, `ReplyToBody`, `ReplyToSender`, `ReplyToIsQuote`
   - Both the user message AND the quoted text are preserved
   - Group and DM quote handling unified

### Tests

- Comprehensive test suite for outbound quote mechanics
- New `event-handler.inbound-contract.test.ts` for inbound quote contract tests
- Refactored `event-handler.quote.test.ts` with edge case coverage
- All tests passing

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Outbound Signal quote-reply parameters were never translated into signal-cli `quote-timestamp` / `quote-author` RPC params, and inbound user quote-replies were dropped or only surfaced as fallback body text. After this fix, `resolveSignalQuoteMetadata` produces the right RPC param shape (and gates out unsafe group quotes), and `describeSignalReplyTarget` returns a structured `SignalReplyTarget` with normalized id, resolved author, body text or media placeholder, and quote kind.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at HEAD `e3740e0223dba46315f0f568d68a14e4ac72fe59` of branch `fix/signal-quote-reply`. Linux 6.12.67, Node v24.15.0, pnpm-driven monorepo. Patched modules in `extensions/signal/src/reply-quote.ts` and `extensions/signal/src/monitor/quote-context.ts` loaded directly with `tsx` from the working tree, and the built CLI (`pnpm openclaw --version`) reports `OpenClaw 2026.5.4 (e3740e0)` confirming the binary is built from the patched commit.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. `pnpm openclaw --version` to confirm the live CLI is built from the patched HEAD.
  2. `node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-pr36630.mts` — driver that loads `extensions/signal/src/reply-quote.ts` and `extensions/signal/src/monitor/quote-context.ts`, then exercises `normalizeSignalQuoteId`, `parseSignalQuoteTimestamp`, `resolveSignalQuoteMetadata` (DM, group, missing author, invalid timestamp), `isSignalGroupTarget`, and `describeSignalReplyTarget` with text-only, image-attachment, missing-author + LRU-resolver, and no-quote payload shapes.
  3. `pnpm test extensions/signal/src/send.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.quote.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.inbound-context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/reply-delivery.test.ts` — full targeted suites for the changed Signal files.
- **Evidence after fix**: Terminal capture from running the patched modules in this worktree.

  Live CLI build proves the binary contains the patched code:

  ```
  $ pnpm openclaw --version
  OpenClaw 2026.5.4 (e3740e0)
  ```

  `normalizeSignalQuoteId` and `parseSignalQuoteTimestamp` console output (real values from running the patched modules):

  ```
  --- normalizeSignalQuoteId ---
    1700000000000 -> "1700000000000"
    "1700000000001" -> "1700000000001"
  ```

## What Problem This Solves

The shared Control UI `clampText` and `truncateText` helpers used raw UTF-16 code-unit slicing. If a limit fell between an astral character's surrogate halves, rendered markdown, tool/activity previews, skill descriptions, or execution-approval text could contain a lone surrogate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both shared formatters now delegate their cut to the repository's canonical `truncateUtf16Safe` helper. Short text, ordinary ASCII truncation, ellipsis placement, and `truncateText` metadata remain unchanged.

The maintainer fixup also corrected the original `clampText` fixture: its emoji began immediately after the old end-exclusive slice boundary, so that test passed before the production fix. The replacement places the high surrogate inside the cut and asserts exact output; 64 lines of manual surrogate scanning were removed.

## User Impact

Control UI truncation no longer produces malformed text when a boundary crosses an emoji or another astral character.

## Evidence

- Exact `clampText` regression: 118 ASCII units followed by an emoji and one trailing character at a 120-unit display cap produces 118 ASCII units plus the ellipsis.
- Exact `truncateText` regression: 120 ASCII units followed by an emoji at a 121-unit cap produces 120 ASCII units and retains the original total of 122.
- Short-text and ordinary ASCII behavior remain covered.
